costs.title: A slow website costs you money, every single day
costs.text: It never shows up on an invoice, but it shows up in your results. Here’s where you’re quietly losing out.

items.title: Visitors who give up
items.text: According to Google, over half of mobile visitors leave if a page takes more than 3 seconds to load.

items.title: Lost Google rankings
items.text: Core Web Vitals are one of the signals Google uses to judge page experience. With equal content, the faster website gets a head start.

items.title: Pricier ads
items.text: Every paid click that lands on a slow page risks going to waste. Google Ads also factors in landing page experience.

Ad campaigns cost more than expected

vitals.title: What happens when someone opens your website
vitals.text: Google measures three moments in your real visitors’ experience. Here they are, frame by frame.
vitals.lcpTitle: LCP · how long the main content takes to show up
vitals.lcpFramesLabel: Example of a fast page loading
vitals.lcpCaption: Example of a fast page: the main content (the green image) appears in 1.4 seconds.
vitals.inpText: The time between a tap and the page reacting. Too slow, and visitors tap twice, lose patience and assume the website is broken.
vitals.clsText: How much the page shifts around as it loads. You know when you go to tap a link and a banner pops up and shoves it down? That.

optimize.title: Where slowdowns hide (and how I get rid of them)
optimize.text: Every website is different: I only touch what needs fixing, starting with what makes the biggest difference.

items.title: Images and video
items.text: Modern formats (WebP, AVIF), the right size for every screen, loaded only when needed.

items.title: CSS and JavaScript
items.text: I strip out what’s not needed, defer what can wait and slim down the rest.

items.title: Fonts
items.text: Self-hosted, with no text jumping around as the page opens.

items.title: Server, caching and CDN
items.text: The right hosting, properly configured caching, compression and content served close to your visitors.

items.title: Third-party scripts
items.text: Chat widgets, maps, videos, pixels and cookie banners, loaded so they never hold the page up.

items.title: WordPress and plugins
items.text: Heavy page builders, plugins you don’t need, a bloated database: I clean it all up without breaking a thing.

faq.title: Questions about speed
faq.text: Can’t see yours? [Drop me a line](#contatti) and I’ll reply by the next business day.

items.question: Do I need a new website to make it fast?
items.answer: Hardly ever. In the vast majority of cases, the big gains come from working on the website you have: images, scripts, caching, plugins. If it has structural limits I’ll tell you straight away, with the alternatives.

items.question: Will I hit 100 on Lighthouse?
items.answer: It depends on the website: themes, plugins and external services sometimes set limits. The check-up gives you a realistic picture of how far we can go, before you commit to anything.

items.question: Could the changes break anything?
items.answer: I work on a copy of your website and check every page before publishing. I always take a full backup, so we can roll back at any time.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: The check-up takes a few business days. The fixes depend on what turns up: the quote gives you timing and costs, at a fixed price.

items.question: When will I see results on Google?
items.answer: Lighthouse scores improve straight away. Real-visitor data, which Google uses for Core Web Vitals, catches up over about 28 days.

items.question: Will my website stay fast?
items.answer: New plugins, unoptimized image uploads and scripts added over time can slow it down again. That’s why I offer monthly monitoring and leave you a few simple rules to follow.
